ca-62nd-rbi-monetary-policy-committee-mp.title: 62nd RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Meeting (August 2026)

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: **Monetary Policy Review → Repo Maintained at 5.25%:**
6-member MPC chaired by Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** kept Repo Rate at **5.25%** with a **Neutral** stance.
External Members: Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof. Ram Singh.
Internal Members: Sanjay Malhotra (Governor), Dr. Poonam Gupta, Indranil Bhattacharyya.

**Core Inflation (FY27):** **4.3%**

ca-62nd-rbi-monetary-policy-committee-mp.contentMarkdown:
### 1. 62nd RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Meeting (August 2026)
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep | **Revision Effort:** ~10 min | **Category:** RBI & Monetary Policy
* **Source:** CGB Mentors & Smartkeeda | **Event Date:** August 3–5, 2026

**What Happened**
* **Monetary Policy Review → Repo Maintained at 5.25%:**
  * 6-member MPC chaired by Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** kept Repo Rate at **5.25%** with a **Neutral** stance.
  * External Members: Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof. Ram Singh.
  * Internal Members: Sanjay Malhotra (Governor), Dr. Poonam Gupta, Indranil Bhattacharyya.

**Must Memorize (Core Exam Numbers)**
* **Policy Rates & Macro Projections Ladder:**
  * **Policy Repo Rate:** **5.25%** *(Unchanged)*
  * **FY27 Real GDP Growth:** **6.7%** (Q₁: 7.0%, Q₂: 6.4%, Q₃: 6.5%, Q₄: 6.8%)
  * **FY27 CPI Inflation:** **5.0%** (earlier 5.1%) (Q₂: 4.7%, Q₃: 5.9%, Q₄: 5.5%)
  * **Core Inflation (FY27):** **4.3%**
  * **External Buffer:** Q1 Gross FDI at **$30.7 Billion**; Forex cover $>10$ months; External debt cover at **90.8%**.
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *Repo: 5.25%  •  FY27 GDP: 6.7%, CPI: 5.0%, Core: 4.3%  •  Forex cover >10 months.*

**Know / Understand**
* Core inflation is anchored at 4.3%, but food supply risks (El Niño disruptions affecting pulses and vegetables) prevent premature monetary easing.
* ⚠️ **Change-Sensitive:** Next MPC meeting scheduled for October 5–7, 2026.

ca-rbi-on-tap-licensing-guidelines-for-u.title: RBI 'On Tap' Licensing Guidelines for Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)
ca-rbi-on-tap-licensing-guidelines-for-u.atomicRecall: RBI 'On Tap' Licensing Guidelines for Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs)

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: **Cooperative Banking Transition → Commercial Bank Conversion:**
RBI released 'On Tap' licensing guidelines allowing eligible primary Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) with multi-state operations to convert into commercial banks.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Conversion Thresholds Ladder:**
**Track Record:** Minimum **10 years** continuous operations.
**Deposit Base:** Minimum **₹10,000 Crore** (audited as of March 31).
**Net Worth:** Minimum **₹300 Crore**.
**CRAR & Asset Quality:** Minimum **12% CRAR**  •  Maximum **3% Net NPA**.
**Financial Trend:** Positive over previous **5 years**.
**Scope & Shareholding:** Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act 2002 units  •  Individual shareholding capped at **5%**.
🎯 **Recap:** *UCB conversion: 10-yr track record  •  ₹10k Cr deposits  •  ₹300 Cr net worth  •  CRAR ≥ 12%$, Net NPA ≤ 3%$.*
knowUnderstandContext: Licensing Architecture: On-tap licensing allows qualified entities meeting capital and governance criteria to apply for UCB licenses continuously rather than waiting for ad-hoc regulatory windows.

ca-rbi-loan-recovery-directions-financed.title: RBI Loan Recovery Directions & Financed Smartphone Lockout Norms
ca-rbi-loan-recovery-directions-financed.atomicRecall: RBI Loan Recovery Directions & Financed Smartphone Lockout Norms

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: **Borrower Protection & Debt Recovery Safeguards:**
Notified directions governing recovery agents and prohibiting predatory device lockouts.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Calling Norms & Smartphone Locks Ladder:**
**Calling Hours:** Strictly **8:00 AM to 7:00 PM** (No calls during bereavement/emergencies).
**Agent Certification:** Mandatory **IIBF Certification**.
**Device Lockout Stages:** No restriction before **30 DPD**; complete restrictions permitted only after **60 DPD**.
**Emergency Safeguard:** Incoming calls, SMS, and emergency SOS **can NEVER be disabled**.
**Restoration:** Unlock within **1 hour** of payment (Delay penalty: **₹250/hour** on bank).
Key Facts: Deferred to **January 1, 2027**; mandatory IIBF agent certification, calling hours 8 am–7 pm, smartphone locking norms.
🎯 **Recap:** *Calling: 8 AM–7 PM  •  Smartphone lockout only after 60 DPD (SOS never disabled)  •  ₹250/hr unlock delay fine.*
knowUnderstandContext: Fair Practices Code: Prohibits lenders and recovery agents from deploying remote handset-locking malware, ensuring borrower dignity and digital privacy.
**Effective Date:** **1 January 2027** | **Source:** CGB Mentors

mustMemorizeFacts: Window: **August 16 to December 31, 2026** (Benchmark: March 31, 2026).
**Category A (untaxed ≤ ₹1 Cr):** **60% effective tax** (30% tax + 30% penalty).
**Category B (taxed/omitted ≤ ₹5 Cr):** **₹1 Lakh flat fee**.
**Operational Window:** **August 16 to December 31, 2026** (Benchmark: **March 31, 2026**).
**Asset Scope:** 4 categories (foreign assets, untaxed foreign income, non-resident assets, omitted FA schedules).
**Form Workflow:** **Form 1** (Declaration)  →  **Form 2** (Determination Order by DG Income Tax Systems).
**Payment Horizon:** **2 months** without interest  →  statutory immunity under Black Money Act 2015.
🎯 **Recap:** *FAST-DS: Aug 16–Dec 31, 2026  •  March 31, 2026 benchmark  •  Form 1  →  Form 2 (2 months to pay).*
knowUnderstandContext: Tax Compliance Mechanism: The Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS) provides a one-time relief window under the Black Money Act for small taxpayers with inadvertent minor foreign asset disclosures.

whatHappened: **Internal Grievance Architecture Overhaul → Unified 2026 Directions:**
RBI issued comprehensive **Reserve Bank of India (Internal Ombudsman) Directions, 2026**, superseding the 2023 Master Direction.
**Effective Date:** Takes effect from **June 30, 2026**.
**Applicability (6 Entity Categories):** (1) Commercial Banks, (2) SFBs, (3) Payments Banks, (4) NBFCs, (5) Non-Bank PPI Issuers, (6) Credit Information Companies (CICs).
mustMemorizeFacts: **Internal Ombudsman (IO) Eligibility & Service Rules Ladder:**
**IO Rank & Experience:** Retired or serving **General Manager (GM)**  •  Minimum **7 years relevant experience**.
**Deputy IO Rank & Experience:** Retired or serving **Deputy General Manager (DGM)**  •  Minimum **5 years relevant experience**.
**Age Ceiling:** Not over **70 years of age** before completion of tenure.
**Tenure Constraints:** Fixed term of **not less than 3 years**, and total tenure **shall not exceed 5 years** (including extensions).
**Unexpected Vacancies:** Must notify RBI within **10 working days** and appoint replacement.
**Automated Escalation & Review Timelines Ladder:**
**Auto-Escalation:** All complaints **partially resolved or wholly rejected** by bank's internal desk are **auto-escalated to the IO**.
**Review Timelines:**
**RBI/NPCI/Card Network Deadline Cases:** IO gets at least **10 days** for review.
**Other Complaints:** Reviewed within **20 days** of receipt.
**Final Reply to Complainant:** Maximum **30 days** from initial complaint receipt.
**Compensation Ceilings under RBI Ombudsman Scheme:**
**Dispute Value:** No monetary ceiling on dispute amount brought before Ombudsman.
**Consequential Loss Compensation:** Up to **₹30 Lakh**.
**Harassment & Mental Anguish Compensation:** Up to **₹3 Lakh**.

🎯 **Recap:** *IO (GM/7 yrs)  •  Dy IO (DGM/5 yrs)  •  Age ≤ 70 yrs  •  Tenure 3–5 yrs  •  Vacancy: 10 days  •  Auto-escalation on rejection  •  Reply ≤ 30 days  •  Compensation: ₹30L loss, ₹3L harassment.*
knowUnderstandContext: The IO serves as an independent mediator between frontline bank support and the external RBI Ombudsman. Auto-escalation prevents frontline staff from unilaterally closing unresolved grievances.
examFocus: Exact eligibility rank (GM for IO, DGM for Dy IO) and experience thresholds (7 years vs 5 years).
Age ceiling (70 years) and tenure constraints (min 3 years, max 5 years).
Auto-escalation trigger: partial resolution or rejection by bank's internal team.
Compensation ceilings: ₹30 lakh (consequential loss) and ₹3 lakh (mental anguish/harassment).

ca-rbi-tightens-related-party-transactio.title: RBI Tightens Related Party Transactions & Credit Risk Norms for Banks and NBFCs
ca-rbi-tightens-related-party-transactio.atomicRecall: RBI Tightens Related Party Transactions & Credit Risk Norms for Banks and NBFCs

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: **Credit Risk Management Reform → Related Party Transaction Oversight:**
RBI amended *Credit Risk Management Directions* for banks and NBFCs, effective **April 1, 2026**.
Harmonizes the definition of "Related Party" with the **Companies Act, 2013** and **IBC**, bringing NBFCs to commercial banking standards.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Definition of Related Party & Lending Scope:**
**Related Party Entities:** Promoters, directors, KMPs, relatives, and shareholders holding **10% or more equity**.
**Reciprocally Related Persons (Banks):** Directors of other banks/FIs, trustees of AIFs and Mutual Funds.
**Lending Scope:** Includes fund-based and non-fund-based credit and debt securities; **explicitly excludes equity investments**.
**Transaction Materiality Approval Thresholds Ladder:**
**Banks > ₹10 Lakh Crore Assets:** Loan $> mathbf{₹50  Crore}$ requires Board approval.
**Banks ₹1 Lakh Cr – ₹10 Lakh Cr Assets:** Threshold is **₹10 Crore**.
**Banks < ₹1 Lakh Crore Assets:** Threshold is **₹5 Crore**.
**Top / Upper Layer NBFCs:** Threshold is **₹10 Crore**.
**Middle Layer NBFCs:** Threshold is **₹5 Crore**.
**Base Layer NBFCs:** Threshold is **₹1 Crore**.
🎯 **Recap:** *RPT rules effective April 1, 2026  •  10%+ equity shareholders  •  Bank approval caps: ₹50 Cr, ₹10 Cr, ₹5 Cr  •  NBFC caps: ₹10 Cr, ₹5 Cr, ₹1 Cr.*
knowUnderstandContext: Prevents siphoning of depositor funds to promoter-controlled shell companies. Asset tiering ensures proportional burden without creating board-level logjams in mega-banks.
examFocus: Materiality threshold matrix across bank asset sizes (₹50 cr, ₹10 cr, ₹5 cr) and NBFC layers (₹10 cr, ₹5 cr, ₹1 cr).
Treatment of equity investments (excluded from lending definition).
Shareholder threshold for related-party tagging (10% or more equity).

ca-dicgc-notifies-risk-based-premium-rbp.contentMarkdown:
### 1. DICGC Notifies Risk-Based Premium (RBP) Framework for Deposit Insurance
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep
* **Category:** BANKING_REGULATION
* **Institution:** RBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-02-08
* **Revision Effort:** ~8 min
* **Status:** NOTIFIED

#### What Happened
* **Deposit Insurance Pricing Reform → Risk-Based Premium (RBP):**
  * DICGC notified implementation of the **Risk-Based Premium (RBP) framework** under **Section 15(1) of the DICGC Act, 1961**.
  * Replaces the flat 12 paise per ₹100 premium system in place since 1962.
  * **Effective Date:** **April 1, 2026** (reviewed every 3 years).

#### Must Memorize
* **Two Risk Assessment Models Ladder:**
  * **Tier 1 Model (SCBs excluding RRBs):** Evaluated on supervisory ratings, quantitative CAMELS parameters, and potential loss to Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF).
  * **Tier 2 Model (RRBs and Co-operative Banks):** Evaluated on quantitative CAMELS parameters and DIF loss risk.
* **Incentive Discount Caps & Formula:**
  * **Risk Model Incentive:** Up to **33.33% discount** over card rate.
  * **Vintage Model Incentive:** Up to **25% discount** for long-term claim-free contributions.
  * **Effective Formula:**
    $$Effective Rate = Card Rate  ×  (1 - Risk Model Discount)  ×  (1 - Vintage Model Discount)$$
* **Exemptions Retaining Flat 12 Paise Card Rate:**
  * **Payments Banks (PBs) & Local Area Banks (LABs):** Retain flat **12 paise per ₹100** rate ($<1%$ of total premiums).
  * **UCBs under SAF / PCA:** Retain flat 12 paise rate until financial year following exit from SAF/PCA.
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *Section 15(1) DICGC Act  •  Effective April 1, 2026  •  Max discounts: 33.33% (Risk), 25% (Vintage)  •  PBs/LABs/PCA banks keep flat 12p rate.*

#### Know / Understand
* Shifts deposit insurance from a mutualized subsidy model to a risk-sensitive discipline aligning premium cost with asset risk and governance health.

#### Exam Focus
* Legal section: Section 15(1) of DICGC Act, 1961.
* Effective date: April 1, 2026 (reviewed every 3 years).
* Maximum incentive caps: 33.33% (Risk Model) and 25% (Vintage Model).
* Entities retaining flat 12 paise card rate: Payments Banks, Local Area Banks, and UCBs under SAF/PCA.

mustMemorizeFacts: **Collateral-Free Lending Parameters Ladder:**

**Voluntary Pledges:** Voluntary borrower pledges of gold/silver are explicitly permitted.

  * Raised the mandatory collateral-free lending ceiling for micro and small enterprises.

#### Must Memorize

  * **PMEGP Linkage:** Mandatory **₹20 Lakh** collateral-free threshold applies across all PMEGP units (KVIC).
  * **Discretionary Limit:** Banks can raise collateral-free limit **up to ₹25 Lakh** for borrowers with sound track records.
  * **Voluntary Pledges:** Voluntary borrower pledges of gold/silver are explicitly permitted.

ca-insolvency-bankruptcy-code-amendment-.atomicRecall: Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2025: Introduction of CIIRP & Structural Timelines

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures
Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: **Insolvency Resolution Modernisation → Creditor-Initiated Insolvency (CIIRP):**
Parliament passed the **IBC (Amendment) Bill, 2025**, introducing 12 structural amendments.
Introduces **Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (CIIRP)** under **Chapter IV-A** of the Code.
mustMemorizeFacts: **CIIRP Parameters & Voting Thresholds Ladder:**
**Initiation Voting Share:** Financial creditors holding **≥ 51%$ of voting share** can initiate CIIRP.
**Resolution Timeline:** Compressed to **150 days** (maximum single extension of **45 days**).
**Debtor-in-Possession Model:** Promoters retain management under continuous Resolution Professional (RP) supervision.
**Admission & Liquidation Timelines Ladder:**
**NCLT Admission/Rejection:** Strictly within **14 days** (mandatory recording of delay reasons).
**Resolution Plan Approval by NCLT:** Strictly within **30 days**.
**CIRP Revival:** Allowed **once before liquidation** within **120 days** of failure.
**Liquidation Completion:** Within **180 days** (max extension **90 days**).
**Liquidator Replacement:** Requires **66% CoC voting majority**.
**Application Withdrawal:** Requires **90% CoC approval** (only after CoC formation, before plans invited).
**Penalties:** Frivolous filings: **₹1 Lakh to ₹2 Crore**  •  Non-compliance: Up to **₹5 Crore or 3x gains/losses**.
🎯 **Recap:** *CIIRP (51% vote, 150+45 days)  •  NCLT admission: 14 days  •  Plan approval: 30 days  •  Liquidation: 180+90 days (66% CoC vote)  •  Withdrawal: 90% CoC vote.*
knowUnderstandContext: CIIRP provides an out-of-court, debtor-in-possession alternative to CIRP, preventing enterprise destruction while empowering lenders to resolve distress rapidly.
examFocus: Voting threshold to initiate CIIRP (51%) and replace liquidator (66%).
CIIRP timeline (150 + 45 days) vs Liquidation timeline (180 + 90 days).
Mandatory admission timeline for NCLT (14 days) and resolution plan approval (30 days).
CoC threshold to approve withdrawal of insolvency application (90%).

#### What Happened

  * Parliament passed the **IBC (Amendment) Bill, 2025**, introducing 12 structural amendments.
  * Introduces **Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (CIIRP)** under **Chapter IV-A** of the Code.

#### Must Memorize
* **CIIRP Parameters & Voting Thresholds Ladder:**
  * **Initiation Voting Share:** Financial creditors holding **≥ 51%$ of voting share** can initiate CIIRP.
  * **Resolution Timeline:** Compressed to **150 days** (maximum single extension of **45 days**).
  * **Debtor-in-Possession Model:** Promoters retain management under continuous Resolution Professional (RP) supervision.
* **Admission & Liquidation Timelines Ladder:**
  * **NCLT Admission/Rejection:** Strictly within **14 days** (mandatory recording of delay reasons).
  * **Resolution Plan Approval by NCLT:** Strictly within **30 days**.
  * **CIRP Revival:** Allowed **once before liquidation** within **120 days** of failure.
  * **Liquidation Completion:** Within **180 days** (max extension **90 days**).
  * **Liquidator Replacement:** Requires **66% CoC voting majority**.
  * **Application Withdrawal:** Requires **90% CoC approval** (only after CoC formation, before plans invited).
  * **Penalties:** Frivolous filings: **₹1 Lakh to ₹2 Crore**  •  Non-compliance: Up to **₹5 Crore or 3x gains/losses**.
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *CIIRP (51% vote, 150+45 days)  •  NCLT admission: 14 days  •  Plan approval: 30 days  •  Liquidation: 180+90 days (66% CoC vote)  •  Withdrawal: 90% CoC vote.*

#### Know / Understand
* CIIRP provides an out-of-court, debtor-in-possession alternative to CIRP, preventing enterprise destruction while empowering lenders to resolve distress rapidly.

ca-rbi-responsible-business-conduct-dire.title: RBI Responsible Business Conduct Directions 2026: Online Fraud Compensation & 2FA Mandate
ca-rbi-responsible-business-conduct-dire.atomicRecall: RBI Responsible Business Conduct Directions 2026: Online Fraud Compensation & 2FA Mandate

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: **Consumer Protection Overhaul → Fraud Relief & Dynamic 2FA:**
RBI issued *Responsible Business Conduct (Third Amendment) Directions, 2026*, effective **July 1, 2026**.
Establishes customer fraud compensation and mandates dynamic Two-Factor Authentication.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Fraud Compensation & Security Mandates Ladder:**
**Small-Value Online Fraud Relief:**
Gross losses up to **₹50,000** eligible for **85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is less** *(once in lifetime)*.
Must be reported within **5 days** to bank and National Cyber Crime Portal / Helpline (**1930**).
**Zero Customer Liability:** 100% reversal if fraud arises from bank deficiency, or third-party breach reported within **5 calendar days**.
**Dynamic 2FA Mandate:** Mandatory 2FA with at least one dynamic factor (OTP, biometric) for domestic digital transactions from **April 1, 2026** (cross-border CNP: **October 1, 2026**).
**Mandatory Instant SMS:** Required for all transactions $> mathbf{₹500}$.
🎯 **Recap:** *Small fraud relief: 85% loss or ₹25,000 (losses up to ₹50k, 5-day report to 1930)  •  Dynamic 2FA from April 1, 2026  •  SMS alerts $>₹500$.*
knowUnderstandContext: Establishes a retail safety net for depositors against phishing and SIM-swap attacks while compelling banks to deploy real-time ML fraud interdiction tools.
examFocus: Small-value fraud compensation cap (85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is lower; once in lifetime).
Maximum gross loss eligible for small fraud relief (₹50,000) and reporting window (5 days; Helpline 1930).
2FA implementation date (April 1, 2026; Cross-border Oct 1, 2026).
Mandatory SMS alert threshold (>₹500).
ca-rbi-responsible-business-conduct-dire.contentMarkdown:
### 3. RBI Responsible Business Conduct Directions 2026: Online Fraud Compensation & 2FA Mandate
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep
* **Category:** BANKING_REGULATION
* **Institution:** RBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-03-08
* **Revision Effort:** ~8 min
* **Status:** NOTIFIED

#### What Happened
* **Consumer Protection Overhaul → Fraud Relief & Dynamic 2FA:**
  * RBI issued *Responsible Business Conduct (Third Amendment) Directions, 2026*, effective **July 1, 2026**.
  * Establishes customer fraud compensation and mandates dynamic Two-Factor Authentication.

#### Must Memorize
* **Fraud Compensation & Security Mandates Ladder:**
  * **Small-Value Online Fraud Relief:**
    * Gross losses up to **₹50,000** eligible for **85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is less** *(once in lifetime)*.
    * Must be reported within **5 days** to bank and National Cyber Crime Portal / Helpline (**1930**).
  * **Zero Customer Liability:** 100% reversal if fraud arises from bank deficiency, or third-party breach reported within **5 calendar days**.
  * **Dynamic 2FA Mandate:** Mandatory 2FA with at least one dynamic factor (OTP, biometric) for domestic digital transactions from **April 1, 2026** (cross-border CNP: **October 1, 2026**).
  * **Mandatory Instant SMS:** Required for all transactions $> mathbf{₹500}$.
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *Small fraud relief: 85% loss or ₹25,000 (losses up to ₹50k, 5-day report to 1930)  •  Dynamic 2FA from April 1, 2026  •  SMS alerts $>₹500$.*

#### Know / Understand
* Establishes a retail safety net for depositors against phishing and SIM-swap attacks while compelling banks to deploy real-time ML fraud interdiction tools.

#### Exam Focus
* Small-value fraud compensation cap (85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is lower; once in lifetime).
* Maximum gross loss eligible for small fraud relief (₹50,000) and reporting window (5 days; Helpline 1930).
* 2FA implementation date (April 1, 2026; Cross-border Oct 1, 2026).
* Mandatory SMS alert threshold (>₹500).

ca-sebi-scale-based-framework-for-market.title: SEBI IT Resilience Index Framework for Market Infrastructure Institutions
ca-sebi-scale-based-framework-for-market.atomicRecall: SEBI IT Resilience Index Framework for Market Infrastructure Institutions

likelyAsks: Global rank of India / benchmark publishing institution

whatHappened: **MII Cybersecurity & Operational Risk Metric → IT Resilience Index (ITRI):**
SEBI notified a standardized **IT Resilience Index (ITRI)** framework for Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs: Stock Exchanges, Depositories, Clearing Corporations).
Measures operational robustness, system uptime, and cybersecurity resilience.
mustMemorizeFacts: **MII Cyber Resilience:**
9-parameter index; system availability and security carry **20% weight each** (half-yearly evaluation).
**ITRI Weightages & Compliance Milestones Ladder:**
**9 Evaluation Parameters & Weights:**
Availability (20%)** & **Security (20%): Highest combined weight (**40%**).
Integrity (10%)**, **Governance (10%)**, **Reliability & Monitoring (10%)**, **Business Continuity (10%)**, **Modularity & Flexibility (10%): Standard core weights (**50%**).
Scalability (5%)** & **Incident Handling (5%): Balance weights (**10%**).
**Early Warning System (EWS):** MIIs must deploy EWS to detect parameter deterioration by **28 February 2027**.
**First Computation Window:** Half-year ended **31 March 2027**.
**Reporting Cycle:** Computed **half-yearly**  •  Submitted within **60 days** of half-year end to SEBI's Standing Committee on Technology (SCOT) and Governing Boards.
**Cyber Incident Reporting:** Integrated with SEBI's portal (`https://iportal.sebi.gov.in`) aligned with Financial Stability Board's **Format for Incident Reporting Exchange (FSB FIRE)**.
🎯 **Recap:** *ITRI for MIIs: 9 parameters (Availability 20%, Security 20%)  •  Half-yearly computation in 60 days  •  EWS by Feb 28, 2027  •  FSB FIRE alignment.*

ca-rbi-finalizes-expected-credit-loss-ec.atomicRecall: RBI Finalizes Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Provisioning Norms (Effective April 1, 2027)

likelyAsks: Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: **Provisioning Model Overhaul → Transition to Expected Losses:**
RBI finalized comprehensive guidelines for commercial banks to transition from the historical incurred-loss model to the forward-looking **Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework**.
**Effective Date:** Takes effect from **April 1, 2027**.
**Objective:** Mandates estimation and provisioning for potential credit losses prior to default, cushioned by a 4-year transition glidepath.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Three-Stage Asset Classification & Provisioning Floors:**
**Stage 1 (Performing Advances):** 12-month expected loss  →  minimum floor of **0.4%** for standard corporate/retail loans.
**Stage 2 (Underperforming / SICR):** Lifetime expected loss (60–90 DPD)  →  minimum floor of **5%**.
**Stage 3 (Impaired / NPAs):** Full lifetime loss provision for loans with objective default evidence (90+ DPD).
**Capital Transition Glidepath → Four-Year Cushion:**
Banks can amortize incremental provisioning over **4 years ending March 31, 2031**.
**CET1 Relief:** Permitted to add back net tax-adjusted provision increase to **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital** until March 31, 2031.
**Three Computational Parameters:**
**PD (Probability of Default):** Likelihood of default over 12 months or lifetime.
**LGD (Loss Given Default):** Percentage of exposure lost if default occurs.
**EAD (Exposure at Default):** Total gross value exposed to default risk.
**Effective Interest Rate (EIR) Mandate:** Transition for all outstanding loans by **March 31, 2030**.
🎯 **Recap:** *ECL effective April 1, 2027  •  Stage 1 (0.4%), Stage 2 (5%), Stage 3 (Full)  •  4-yr CET1 add-back to March 31, 2031  •  EIR deadline 2030.*

ca-rbi-finalizes-expected-credit-loss-ec.contentMarkdown:
### 1. RBI Finalizes Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Provisioning Norms (Effective April 1, 2027)
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep
* **Category:** BANKING_REGULATION
* **Institution:** RBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-04-12
* **Revision Effort:** ~8 min
* **Status:** NOTIFIED

#### What Happened
* **Provisioning Model Overhaul → Transition to Expected Losses:**
  * RBI finalized comprehensive guidelines for commercial banks to transition from the historical incurred-loss model to the forward-looking **Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework**.
  * **Effective Date:** Takes effect from **April 1, 2027**.
  * **Objective:** Mandates estimation and provisioning for potential credit losses prior to default, cushioned by a 4-year transition glidepath.

#### Must Memorize
* **Three-Stage Asset Classification & Provisioning Floors:**
  * **Stage 1 (Performing Advances):** 12-month expected loss  →  minimum floor of **0.4%** for standard corporate/retail loans.
  * **Stage 2 (Underperforming / SICR):** Lifetime expected loss (60–90 DPD)  →  minimum floor of **5%**.
  * **Stage 3 (Impaired / NPAs):** Full lifetime loss provision for loans with objective default evidence (90+ DPD).
* **Capital Transition Glidepath → Four-Year Cushion:**
  * Banks can amortize incremental provisioning over **4 years ending March 31, 2031**.
  * **CET1 Relief:** Permitted to add back net tax-adjusted provision increase to **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital** until March 31, 2031.
* **Three Computational Parameters:**
  * **PD (Probability of Default):** Likelihood of default over 12 months or lifetime.
  * **LGD (Loss Given Default):** Percentage of exposure lost if default occurs.
  * **EAD (Exposure at Default):** Total gross value exposed to default risk.
* **Effective Interest Rate (EIR) Mandate:** Transition for all outstanding loans by **March 31, 2030**.
* 🎯 **Recap:** *ECL effective April 1, 2027  •  Stage 1 (0.4%), Stage 2 (5%), Stage 3 (Full)  •  4-yr CET1 add-back to March 31, 2031  •  EIR deadline 2030.*

#### Know / Understand
* Incurred loss recognized provisions only after an asset turned NPA. ECL requires dynamic statistical provisioning based on forward-looking macroeconomic deterioration, preventing balance sheet shocks.

#### Exam Focus
* 3 stages of ECL classification (Stage 1: 12-month loss / 0.4%, Stage 2: Lifetime loss / 5%, Stage 3: Full lifetime loss).
* 4-year transition window and CET1 add-back deadline (March 31, 2031).
* 3 core parameters: PD, LGD, EAD.
* EIR transition deadline: March 31, 2030.

ca-rbi-finalizes-revised-lending-housing.title: RBI Finalizes Revised Lending & Housing Loan Norms for Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs)
ca-rbi-finalizes-revised-lending-housing.atomicRecall: RBI Finalizes Revised Lending & Housing Loan Norms for Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs)

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: **Cooperative Lending Framework → Unsecured Caps & Housing Limits:**
RBI issued final revised lending directions for Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs).
Enforces aggregate/individual unsecured exposure limits and restricts housing loan tenures and moratoria.
**Effective Date:** Takes effect from **October 1, 2026**.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Unsecured Lending Ceilings Ladder:**
**Aggregate Unsecured Cap:** Capped at **20% of total loans and advances** *(shifted from earlier 10% of total assets)*.
**Tier-Specific Individual Ceilings:**
**Tier-1 UCBs:** Maximum **₹5 Lakh** per borrower
**Tier-2 UCBs:** Maximum **₹7.5 Lakh** per borrower
**Tier-3 & Tier-4 UCBs:** Maximum **₹10 Lakh** per borrower
**Small PSL Exemption:** Unsecured loans ≤ mathbf{₹50,000}$ qualifying as PSL are excluded from the 20% cap for ECBA-compliant UCBs.
**Housing Loan Limits for Tier-1 & Tier-2 UCBs:**
**Maximum Tenure:** Capped at **20 years** (inclusive of moratorium).
**Moratorium Cap:** Permitted **only for under-construction properties up to 24 months** *(prohibited for ready-to-move purchases)*.
🎯 **Recap:** *UCB unsecured cap: 20% total loans  •  Tier-1 (₹5L), Tier-2 (₹7.5L), Tier-3/4 (₹10L)  •  Housing tenure ≤ 20 yrs  •  Moratorium ≤ 24 mo.*
knowUnderstandContext: Restricts unsecured risk concentration in smaller cooperative banks while ensuring micro-credit flow and preventing maturity mismatches in urban housing loans.
examFocus: Aggregate unsecured lending cap (20% of total loans).
Individual unsecured caps across UCB Tiers: Tier-1 (₹5L), Tier-2 (₹7.5L), Tier-3/4 (₹10L).
Small PSL loan exclusion threshold (₹50,000).
Housing loan tenure cap for Tier-1/2 UCBs (20 years) and maximum construction moratorium (24 months).
Effective date: October 1, 2026.

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

whatHappened: **Forex Market Liberalization → Forex Correspondent Model:**
Overhauled authorization framework under **FEMA (Authorized Persons) Regulations, 2026**.
Introduced the **Forex Correspondent (FxC)** model allowing AD-I and AD-II entities to appoint agents for retail forex operations.
mustMemorizeFacts: **FxC Model & Capital Requirements Ladder:**
**Parent Entities:** AD Category-I and AD Category-II can appoint FxCs under principal-agent model.
**Permitted FxC Scope:** (1) Purchase FX notes/coins/travellers' cheques; (2) Sell FX notes/cheques for private/business travel; (3) Act as MTSS sub-agents.
**AD Category-II Cap:** Capped at **₹25 Lakh per foreign trade transaction**.
**Minimum Net Worth:** **₹10 Crore (AD-II)**  •  **₹2 Crore (AD-III)**.
**2-Year Turnover Mandate:** Must achieve and maintain annual turnover of **₹50 Crore (AD-II)** and **₹10 Crore (FFMCs)** within 2 years.
🎯 **Recap:** *AD-I & AD-II can appoint FxCs  •  AD-II cap: ₹25L/txn  •  Net worth: AD-II ₹10 Cr, AD-III ₹2 Cr  •  Turnover: ₹50 Cr / ₹10 Cr.*
knowUnderstandContext: Expands retail forex reach across non-metro towns through agent networks while anchoring regulatory accountability to parent banks.
examFocus: Eligible parent entities to appoint FxCs (AD-I and AD-II).
AD Category-II transaction ceiling (₹25 lakh per trade transaction).
Minimum net worth: ₹10 crore (AD-II) and ₹2 crore (AD-III).
Minimum 2-year turnover thresholds: ₹50 crore (AD-II) and ₹10 crore (FFMC).

ca-rbi-discontinues-mandatory-investment.atomicRecall: RBI Discontinues Mandatory Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR) for Banks

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: **Prudential Reserve Rationalization → IFR Discontinued:**
Discontinued mandatory creation and maintenance of **Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR)** by commercial banks.
**Effective Date:** Came into force on **May 18, 2026**.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Accounting Treatment & Balance Transfers:**
Existing IFR balances as of May 17, 2026 transferred **'below the line' to Statutory Reserve, General Reserve, or Balance of Profit & Loss Account**.
**Foreign Banks in India:** Transferred directly to Indian books' statutory reserves or non-repatriable remittable surplus.
**SFBs and Payments Banks:** Transfers must come from net profit after mandatory statutory appropriations.
🎯 **Recap:** *IFR discontinued from May 18, 2026  •  Existing balances transferred below the line to Statutory/General Reserves.*
knowUnderstandContext: IFR was created to absorb yield volatility in AFS/HFT portfolios. With modern mark-to-market accounting under Basel III, standalone IFR became redundant.
examFocus: Effective date of IFR discontinuation: May 18, 2026.
Accounting treatment of existing IFR balances (transferred 'below the line' to Statutory/General Reserve or P&L).
Treatment for foreign bank branches.

Reviewed 1-year progress showing over **72 lakh first-time formal employees** enrolled.
Official Union Cabinet sanctioned budgetary outlay is **₹99,446 Crore** (spanning FY 2025-26 to FY 2031-32) for the Employment-Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme.
mustMemorizeFacts: **PM-VBRY Structure & Outlay Ladder:**
**Official Sanctioned Outlay:** **₹99,446 Crore** (FY 2025-26 to FY 2031-32).
**Employment Target:** Creation of **3.5 Crore formal jobs** (targeting **1.92 Crore first-time entrants**).
**Implementation Window:** **1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027** (2-year registration period).
**Part A (First-Time Employees earning $≤ ₹1L/month$):**
**1 month EPF wage up to ₹15,000**, paid in **2 equal instalments** (at 6 months & 12 months continuous service + financial literacy module).
**Part B (Employers):**
**Up to ₹3,000/month per additional employee for 2 years** (extended to **3rd and 4th years for manufacturing**).
**Digital Verification:** UAN Face Authentication on **UMANG App** and direct DBT.
🎯 **Recap:** *PM-VBRY: ₹99,446 Cr official outlay  •  3.5 Cr jobs  •  ₹15k employee bonus (in 2 instalments at 6m & 12m)  •  ₹3k/mo employer incentive.*
knowUnderstandContext: **Provenance & Audit History (Phase 4 Correction — 3 Sep 2026):**
*Originally Sourced Claim*: ₹1,07,000 Crore Scheme Outlay (CGB Mentors Part 1 / Smartkeeda W2).
*Authoritative Primary Reference*: Union Cabinet Resolution / Press Information Bureau (PIB) (Ministry of Labour & Employment).
*Correction Reason*: Coaching note reported unverified pre-Cabinet draft industry estimates of ₹1,07,000 Cr; official sanctioned Cabinet outlay is ₹99,446 Cr (discrepancy of ₹7,554 Cr corrected).

whatHappened: **Capital Market Modernisation → Rupee Fees & Intraday MF Liquidity:**
Replaced USD-denominated fee structures with Rupee-denominated regime for FPIs and FVCIs.

mustMemorizeFacts: **Rupee FPI Fees & Market Reforms Ladder:**
**FPI Registration Fees:** Cat-I FPI/FVCI registration charge revised to **₹2.3 Lakh** (from $2,500); Application fee: **₹90,000** (from $1,000).

**MF Intraday Borrowing:** Allowed for pay-in/pay-out mismatches (operates **over and above** the 20% NAV redemption borrowing limit).
**Depository IPF Expenses:** Capped at **5% of annual income** (**≥ 95%$** ploughed back into corpus).
**MF-Only PMS:** Proposed ₹25 Lakh ticket size, ₹2 Crore net worth, and 2.5% AUM fee cap.
🎯 **Recap:** *FPI fees de-dollarized: ₹2.3L registration / ₹90k application  •  MF intraday borrowing permitted  •  IPF expense cap: 5%.*
knowUnderstandContext: Eliminates operational frictions in multi-market T+1 settlement cycles for mutual funds while de-dollarizing regulatory fees in Indian capital markets.

whatHappened: **Bank Governance & Assurance Functions → Independent Executive Oversight:**
Consolidated directions for CRO, CCO, and Head of Internal Audit (HIA), effective **January 1, 2027**.

**Commercial Bank Governance Architecture → Independent Control Heads:**
Master directions effective **January 1, 2027** establish protected hierarchies for Risk, Compliance, and Audit.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Governance Safeguards & Model Risk Ladder:**
**Fixed Statutory Tenure:** CRO, CCO, and HIA must have minimum tenure of **at least 3 years**.
**Removal Approval:** Premature exit requires explicit **Board of Directors approval**  •  Reported to RBI within **5 working days**.
**Model Risk Management Framework (MRMF):** Mandatory board-approved MRMF for AI/ML credit scoring with **kill-switch controls** and human validation.
**Incentive Bans:** Direct manufacturer incentives/gifts to bank staff strictly prohibited; mis-selling assessed based on customer profile at time of sale.
**Mandatory Control Heads & Governance Rules Ladder:**
**3 Mandatory Control Heads:** (1) CRO, (2) CCO, (3) Head of Internal Audit (HIA).
**Hierarchy:** Senior officials **not more than 2 levels below MD & CEO**.

* Under **Article 124(1)** of the Constitution of India, parliamentary legislation is required to alter Supreme Court judge strength.

* **Constitutional & Service Rules:**
  * **Article:** **Article 124(1)**
  * **Retirement Age:** **65 years** for Supreme Court Judges *(vs 62 years for High Court Judges)*.
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *Sanctioned strength: 39 judges (38 + CJI)  •  Article 124(1)  •  Retirement age: 65 years.*

* New sanctioned strength of Supreme Court: **39 judges**.

ca-rbi-increases-borrowing-limits-agains.atomicRecall: RBI Increases Borrowing Limits Against Securities: ₹1 Crore for Shares & ₹25 Lakh for IPOs

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures
Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

whatHappened: **Regulatory Revision → Capital Market Exposure Architecture:**
**Objective:** Substantially enhance individual borrowing ceilings for capital market participation while establishing macroprudential systemic safeguards.
**Implementation Timeline:** Deferred to **July 1, 2026** (to allow operational transition across core banking systems).
mustMemorizeFacts: **Borrowing Ceilings Revision → System-Wide Risk Architecture:**
**Loans Against Shares / REITs / InvITs:** Raised from ₹20 lakh  →  **₹1 Crore per borrower**
**IPO / FPO / ESOP Subscriptions:** Raised from ₹10 lakh  →  **₹25 Lakh per individual**
**Scope of Limits:** Converted to **aggregate system-wide cap across all banks** *(prevents multi-bank limit circumvention)*
**Listed Debt Securities:** Regulatory ceiling on bank lending **completely removed**
**Mandatory Margins:** **50%** (Physical shares)  •  **25%** (Demat shares)
**Timeline:** Effective **July 1, 2026**
🎯 **Recap:** *Shares ₹1 Cr  •  IPO ₹25L  •  Margins 50%/25%  •  Effective July 1, 2026.*
knowUnderstandContext: **Systemic Risk Mitigation → Single-Borrower PAN Tracking:**
Previously, retail investors could circumvent exposure caps by borrowing ₹20 lakh each from multiple banks simultaneously.
The PAN-linked system-wide ceiling of ₹1 crore (and ₹25 lakh for IPOs) provides liquidity while preventing overleveraged speculative bubbles.
examFocus: Loans against shares ceiling: **₹1 crore per borrower** (earlier ₹20 lakh).
IPO/FPO/ESOP financing limit: **₹25 lakh per individual** (earlier ₹10 lakh).
System-wide aggregate cap rule across entire banking sector.
Margin floors: **50% for physical shares** and **25% for demat shares**.
Implementation effective date: **July 1, 2026**.
ca-rbi-increases-borrowing-limits-agains.contentMarkdown:
### 1. RBI Increases Borrowing Limits Against Securities: ₹1 Crore for Shares & ₹25 Lakh for IPOs
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep
* **Category:** BANKING_REGULATION
* **Institution:** RBI
* **Event Date:** 2026-04-03
* **Revision Effort:** ~8 min
* **Status:** NOTIFIED

#### What Happened
* **Regulatory Revision → Capital Market Exposure Architecture:**
  * **Objective:** Substantially enhance individual borrowing ceilings for capital market participation while establishing macroprudential systemic safeguards.
  * **Implementation Timeline:** Deferred to **July 1, 2026** (to allow operational transition across core banking systems).

#### Must Memorize
* **Borrowing Ceilings Revision → System-Wide Risk Architecture:**
  * **Loans Against Shares / REITs / InvITs:** Raised from ₹20 lakh  →  **₹1 Crore per borrower**
  * **IPO / FPO / ESOP Subscriptions:** Raised from ₹10 lakh  →  **₹25 Lakh per individual**
  * **Scope of Limits:** Converted to **aggregate system-wide cap across all banks** *(prevents multi-bank limit circumvention)*
  * **Listed Debt Securities:** Regulatory ceiling on bank lending **completely removed**
  * **Mandatory Margins:** **50%** (Physical shares)  •  **25%** (Demat shares)
  * **Timeline:** Effective **July 1, 2026**
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *Shares ₹1 Cr  •  IPO ₹25L  •  Margins 50%/25%  •  Effective July 1, 2026.*

#### Know / Understand
* **Systemic Risk Mitigation → Single-Borrower PAN Tracking:**
  * Previously, retail investors could circumvent exposure caps by borrowing ₹20 lakh each from multiple banks simultaneously.
  * The PAN-linked system-wide ceiling of ₹1 crore (and ₹25 lakh for IPOs) provides liquidity while preventing overleveraged speculative bubbles.

#### Exam Focus
* Loans against shares ceiling: **₹1 crore per borrower** (earlier ₹20 lakh).
* IPO/FPO/ESOP financing limit: **₹25 lakh per individual** (earlier ₹10 lakh).
* System-wide aggregate cap rule across entire banking sector.
* Margin floors: **50% for physical shares** and **25% for demat shares**.
* Implementation effective date: **July 1, 2026**.

mustMemorizeFacts: **Must Memorize Facts:**
**Digital Payment Security → Mandatory Multi-Factor Verification:**
**Mandatory Scope:** All domestic online transactions (UPI, credit/debit cards, prepaid mobile wallets).
**Authentication Mechanism:** Single OTP no longer sufficient  →  requires at least **two distinct factors** (e.g., PIN/password + biometric fingerprint/facial scan or OTP).
**Systemic Liability:** Financial institutions strictly liable for unauthorized fraud arising from security/system lapses.
**International Roadmap:** Phased extension to cross-border card transactions by **October 2026**.
🎯 **Recap:** *2FA mandatory for all digital channels  •  Multi-factor beyond standalone OTP  •  Oct 2026 cross-border deadline.*
**Exam Focus:** Mandatory 2FA for all digital payment channels; multi-factor verification beyond standalone OTP; October 2026 international transaction deadline.

ca-national-administrative-initiatives-r.title: National & Administrative Initiatives Roster (April 2026)

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures
Implementing nodal ministry or statutory agency
Regulatory effective date / compliance timeline

mustMemorizeFacts: **MoPNG National PNG Drive 2.0 → Gas Economy Target:**
Extended till June 30, 2026 by PNGRB to scale natural gas share in India's energy basket to **15% by 2030** (>3.1 lakh connections gasified in March 2026).
🎯 **Recap:** *PNG Drive 2.0 extended to June 2026  •  15% natural gas target by 2030.*
**DoT SIM-Binding Deadline Extension → Fraud Safeguards:**
Extended OTT platform SIM-binding deadline to **December 31, 2026** (WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal); revoked mandatory 6-hour web auto-logout in favor of risk-based fraud triggers.
🎯 **Recap:** *SIM-binding deadline: Dec 31, 2026  •  6-hour logout rule revoked.*
**MoSPI SDG Dashboard & e-Sankhyiki Portal:**
Developed in partnership with UN Resident Coordinator Office (UNRCO) for tracking National Indicator Framework time-series data.
🎯 **Recap:** *e-Sankhyiki & SDG Dashboard launched by MoSPI + UNRCO.*
**Nagoya Protocol Compliance Leadership → 56% Global Share:**
India issued 3,561 Internationally Recognized Certificates of Compliance (IRCCs) under Biological Diversity Act 2002 (**56% of global 6,311 IRCCs**; France #2 with 964).
🎯 **Recap:** *India accounts for 56% of all global IRCC biodiversity certificates.*
**Tea Board "Tea Mark" Quality Certification:**
Rolled out voluntary supply-chain traceability certification under Tea (Marketing) Control Order, 2003 (India is 2nd largest global tea producer / 1st in black tea).
🎯 **Recap:** *Tea Mark certification launched for supply-chain traceability.*
**NMDC Iron Ore Landmark → 50 MT Milestone:**
Produced **53.15 MT iron ore in FY26 (+21%)**, becoming 1st mining company in India to cross 50 MT annual milestone (Kirandul, Bacheli, Donimalai).
🎯 **Recap:** *NMDC produced 53.15 MT iron ore in FY26 (1st Indian firm >50 MT).*
**MHA Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) Reclassification:**

Total LWE-affected districts remained at 38 under SRE Scheme; active red corridor contracted to **2 districts ('LWE Affected')** and 35 'Legacy & Thrust' districts (₹1,685.65 Cr released over 5 years).
🎯 **Recap:** *LWE active core down to 2 districts  •  35 legacy/thrust districts.*
**Indian Railways Asset Monetisation Record:**
Earned record **₹6,735 Crore from scrap disposal in FY26** (+12% above ₹6,000 Cr target) across 5,053 e-auctions (South Central Railway top at ₹641.92 Cr).
🎯 **Recap:** *Railways earned record ₹6,735 Cr from scrap disposal in FY26.*
**Customs Duty Exemption on 40 Petrochemicals:**
Full basic customs duty waiver till June 30, 2026 on 40 critical feedstocks (methanol, toluene, styrene, MEG) with ₹1,800 Crore forgone revenue.
🎯 **Recap:** *Customs duty waived on 40 petrochemical feedstocks till June 2026.*
**NCERT Granted Deemed University Status:**
Ministry of Education and UGC granted deemed-to-be-university status under **'De Novo'** category to NCERT and its 6 constituent regional units (RIEs).
🎯 **Recap:** *NCERT granted Deemed University status under De Novo category.*
**Namo Drone Didi SHG Pilot Standings:**
**Karnataka leads India with 145 trained women SHG drone pilots** under ₹1,261 Crore scheme (Prayagraj top district with 16 pilots; 15,000 drone target).
🎯 **Recap:** *Namo Drone Didi: Karnataka #1 (145 pilots)  •  15,000 drone target.*
**India Annual Wind Capacity Addition Record:**
Installed record **6.05 GW wind capacity in FY26 (+46% YoY)**, taking cumulative installed wind power capacity past 56 GW (India ranks 4th globally).
🎯 **Recap:** *Record 6.05 GW wind added in FY26  •  Cumulative wind capacity: 56 GW (#4 globally).*
**Amul Reaches ₹1 Trillion Turnover:**
Amul/GCMMF became India's 1st FMCG enterprise to cross ₹1 lakh crore turnover in FY26 (reported revenue ₹73,450 Cr, +11.4% YoY).
🎯 **Recap:** *Amul crossed ₹1 Trillion total group turnover in FY26.*
**ICAR Task Force on Agricultural Resilience:**
Established Special Task Force under DARE/ICAR to scale 'Mera Gaon Mera Gaurav' across 100 aspirational districts and promote Direct Seeding of Rice (DSR).
🎯 **Recap:** *ICAR task force on DSR and Mera Gaon Mera Gaurav in 100 districts.*
**Skills Outcomes Fund (₹530 Cr):**
Launched by MSDE and NSDC under outcomes-based financing (OBF) to train 2 lakh youth across BFSI, IT-ITeS, and Green Jobs.
🎯 **Recap:** *₹530 Cr Skills Outcomes Fund for 2 lakh youth by MSDE/NSDC.*
**Minimum Export Price on Natural Honey:**
Extended floor price of **$1,400 per metric ton** until December 31, 2026 (ITC HS 04090000) under National Beekeeping & Honey Mission.
🎯 **Recap:** *Natural honey MEP of $1,400/MT extended to Dec 31, 2026.*
**GeM Womaniya Initiative FY26 Volume:**
Secured **13.7 lakh public procurement orders** across >2 lakh registered women-led Micro & Small Enterprises.
🎯 **Recap:** *GeM Womaniya: 13.7 lakh orders across >2 lakh women MSEs.*
**Rajya Sabha Panel of Vice-Chairpersons Reconstituted:**
6 members nominated by Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan: Dinesh Sharma, S. Phangnon Konyak, Ghanshyam Tiwari (BJP); Phulo Devi Netam (INC); M. Thambidurai (AIADMK); Sasmit Patra (BJD).
🎯 **Recap:** *6-member Rajya Sabha panel of vice-chairpersons reconstituted.*
**MeitY AI Governance Group (AIGEG) & TPEC:**
Constituted AI Governance and Economic Group chaired by Ashwini Vaishnaw, supported by Technology and Policy Expert Committee (TPEC) chaired by MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan.
🎯 **Recap:** *AIGEG chaired by Ashwini Vaishnaw  •  TPEC chaired by S. Krishnan.*
**Tata Semiconductor Dholera SEZ Notified:**
Notified 66.17-hectare SEZ for Tata Electronics-PSMC Taiwan **₹91,000 Crore semiconductor fab** (50,000 wafers/month, commercial chips by Dec 2026).
🎯 **Recap:** *Dholera SEZ notified for Tata-PSMC ₹91,000 Cr semiconductor plant.*
**Central Government DA/DR 2% Hike:**
Approved 2% Dearness Allowance/Dearness Relief hike effective Jan 1, 2026 (raising DA to **60% of basic pay**, costing ₹6,791.24 Cr annually).
🎯 **Recap:** *Central DA/DR hiked by 2% to 60% of basic pay.*
**MoEFCC-NBA Grassroots Biodiversity Project:**
5-year $4.88 million project with GEF/UNDP across Sathyamangalam (TN) and Nokrek/Garo Hills (Meghalaya) landscapes.
🎯 **Recap:** *$4.88M biodiversity project in TN and Meghalaya.*
**Vibrant Village Programme-II in J&K:**
6 border villages in Kathua district (Bobiya, Kadyala, Gajnal, Karol Krishna, Rathua, Gujjar Chak) covered under VVP-II (₹6,839 Cr outlay).
🎯 **Recap:** *6 Kathua border villages added to VVP-II.*
**Supreme Court 'Right to Safe Road Travel' Ruling:**
Bench ruled Right to Safe Road Travel is an integral part of **Article 21** (*'In Re: Phalodi Accident'*), ordering removal of NH encroachments within 60 days.
🎯 **Recap:** *Right to Safe Road Travel ruled part of Article 21 by SC.*
**Uttar Pradesh 'Jal Arpan' 10-Year O&M Warranty:**
UP became 1st state to mandate **10-year contractor O&M warranty** for rural piped water supply under Jal Jeevan Mission.
🎯 **Recap:** *UP mandates 10-year O&M warranty for rural piped water.*
**SkyHop Aviation Seaplane AOC:**
DGCA granted commercial Air Operator Certificate to SkyHop Aviation using DHC-6 Twin Otter aircraft to connect 5 Lakshadweep islands.
🎯 **Recap:** *SkyHop Aviation granted AOC for Lakshadweep seaplane operations.*
**Ladakh District Expansion:**
Approved creation of **5 new districts** (Nubra, Sham, Changthang, Zanskar, Drass), expanding Ladakh from 2 to 7 administrative districts.
🎯 **Recap:** *Ladakh expanded from 2 to 7 districts (5 new districts).*
**Punjab 'Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna':**
Approved **₹1,000/month** assistance for women (**₹1,500/month for SC women**) with ₹9,300 Crore budget allocation.
🎯 **Recap:** *Punjab monthly aid: ₹1,000 for women, ₹1,500 for SC women.*
**Andhra Pradesh Weaver Power Subsidy Scheme:**
₹150 Crore scheme providing up to **200 units/mo free electricity for handlooms** and **500 units/mo for powerlooms**, plus ₹4,000 weaver pension.
🎯 **Recap:** *AP free power: 200 units (handlooms), 500 units (powerlooms).*
**AICTE-VAANI 3rd Edition:**
₹4 Crore annual scheme supporting 200 conferences in 22 regional languages across 16 emerging tech domains.
🎯 **Recap:** *AICTE-VAANI: ₹4 Cr/yr across 200 regional language conferences.*
**CAPF General Administration Act 2026:**
Notified statutory quota reserving **50% IG, 67% ADG, and 100% SDG/DG posts** across 7 CAPFs for IPS officers on deputation.
🎯 **Recap:** *CAPF quota: 50% IG, 67% ADG, 100% DG for IPS officers.*
**Meghalaya Official Languages Ordinance 2026:**
Conferred official language status on **Khasi and Garo** alongside English.
🎯 **Recap:** *Khasi & Garo declared official languages of Meghalaya.*
**India Withdraws COP 33 (2028) Hosting Bid:**
Formally withdrew bid to host 2028 UN Climate Summit, leaving South Korea as sole Asia-Pacific bidder.
🎯 **Recap:** *India withdrew COP 33 (2028) hosting proposal.*

ca-dgft-amends-foreign-trade-policy-ftp-.title: DGFT Amends Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023: Global Rupee Invoicing & ACU Settlement Overhaul
ca-dgft-amends-foreign-trade-policy-ftp-.atomicRecall: DGFT Amends Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023: Global Rupee Invoicing & ACU Settlement Overhaul

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

whatHappened: **International Trade Settlement in INR → FTP 2023 Amendment:**
DGFT amended two core provisions of **Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023** to facilitate export invoicing and receipt of payments directly in Indian Rupees (₹).
Aligned with RBI's **Foreign Exchange Management (Manner of Receipt and Payment) Regulations, 2023**.
mustMemorizeFacts: **Rupee Invoicing & ACU Framework Ladder:**
**Non-ACU Countries (Global Scope):**
Export contracts and invoices can now be denominated in **Indian Rupees (₹)** or any foreign currency.
Eliminates earlier mandatory requirement that proceeds must be in freely convertible foreign currency.
**Lines of Credit (LoC) & EXIM Bank Financing:**
Exports financed under **Government of India Lines of Credit (LoC)** or **EXIM Bank** can be denominated and settled in INR.
**Asian Clearing Union (ACU) Rules:**
**Established:** **1974**  •  **Members (9):** Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka.
**Settlement Mechanism:** Regional net obligation settlement through central banks.
**Rule for ACU:** Invoicing/contracts generally in ACU-determined currencies, but **may also be settled in INR as per specific RBI directions**.
🎯 **Recap:** *FTP 2023 amended: Global exports can be invoiced in INR  •  EXIM/GoI LoC exports eligible  •  Aligned with FEMA 2023  •  ACU (9 members, est 1974).*
knowUnderstandContext: Boosts rupee internationalisation by removing regulatory friction for overseas buyers seeking to settle trades via Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) and bilateral local currency mechanisms.

* **Rupee Invoicing & ACU Framework Ladder:**
  * **Non-ACU Countries (Global Scope):**
    * Export contracts and invoices can now be denominated in **Indian Rupees (₹)** or any foreign currency.
    * Eliminates earlier mandatory requirement that proceeds must be in freely convertible foreign currency.
  * **Lines of Credit (LoC) & EXIM Bank Financing:**
    * Exports financed under **Government of India Lines of Credit (LoC)** or **EXIM Bank** can be denominated and settled in INR.
  * **Asian Clearing Union (ACU) Rules:**
    * **Established:** **1974**  •  **Members (9):** Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka.
    * **Settlement Mechanism:** Regional net obligation settlement through central banks.
    * **Rule for ACU:** Invoicing/contracts generally in ACU-determined currencies, but **may also be settled in INR as per specific RBI directions**.
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *FTP 2023 amended: Global exports can be invoiced in INR  •  EXIM/GoI LoC exports eligible  •  Aligned with FEMA 2023  •  ACU (9 members, est 1974).*

**Know / Understand**
* Boosts rupee internationalisation by removing regulatory friction for overseas buyers seeking to settle trades via Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) and bilateral local currency mechanisms.

mustMemorizeFacts: **MCI Governance & Mediation Timelines Ladder:**

ca-unified-payments-interface-upi-10-yea.title: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) 10-Year Decadal Assessment: 66 Cr Daily Txns & ₹314 Lakh Crore Volume
ca-unified-payments-interface-upi-10-yea.atomicRecall: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) 10-Year Decadal Assessment: 66 Cr Daily Txns & ₹314 Lakh Crore Volume

likelyAsks: Financial outlay / budgetary allocation figures

mustMemorizeFacts: **Decadal Digital Payment Expansion Milestone:**

India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI), launched on August 25, 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) under RBI regulatory oversight, completed **10 years of operation**, processing over **66 crore transactions daily** and commanding an **84% share** of India’s overall digital retail payments volume.
**Transaction Velocity & Volume/Value Matrix:**
**Annual Volume Surge:** Expanded from **1.78 crore transactions (FY17)** to **over 24,162 crore transactions (FY26)**  →  Compound Annual Growth Rate (**CAGR**) of **188%** (~13,000-fold surge).
**Annual Value Surge:** Increased from **₹0.07 lakh crore (FY17)** to **~₹314 lakh crore (FY26)** (>4,000-fold surge).
**Bank Network Adoption:** Grew from **21 live banks at launch** (44 at end-FY17) to **703 live member banks in FY26** (spanning PSBs, private, SFBs, payment, and cooperative banks).
**Person-to-Merchant (P2M) Split:** Accounts for **63% of overall volume**, but only **29% of overall value** (routine retail utility).
**Micro-Payment Concentration:** Sub-₹500 transactions represent **86% of total P2M volume**.
**Person-to-Person (P2P) Split:** Accounts for **37% of volume** and **71% of total transaction value**.
**Institutional Leadership:** NPCI MD & CEO — Dilip Asbe | Chairman — Ajay Kumar Choudhary | Headquarters — Mumbai.
🎯 **Recap:** *UPI 10 yrs  •  66 Cr daily txns  •  FY26: 24,162 Cr vol (CAGR 188%) / ₹314 Lakh Cr val  •  703 banks  •  84% digital share.*
knowUnderstandContext: **High-Velocity Micro-Payments vs. High-Value Settlement:**

UPI's primary role has evolved into cash replacement for daily micro-commerce ($86\%$ under ₹500), while high-value commercial transfers drive P2P value ($71\%$). This volume asymmetry is why NPCI emphasizes lightweight architectures (UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay) to prevent core banking core system overloads.
ca-unified-payments-interface-upi-10-yea.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Unified Payments Interface (UPI) 10-Year Decadal Assessment: 66 Cr Daily Txns & ₹314 Lakh Crore Volume
- **Category**: `DIGITAL_PAYMENTS`
- **Institution**: `NPCI`
- **Priority**: `P1_CRITICAL_DEEP`
- **Date**: `2026-08-25`
- **Target Exams**: `SBI PO Mains, IBPS PO Mains`
- **Revision Effort**: `~10 min`
- **Source**: `Smartkeeda (Aug W4 2026)`

#### Performance & Decadal Architecture
* **Decadal Digital Payment Expansion Milestone:**
  * India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI), launched on August 25, 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) under RBI regulatory oversight, completed **10 years of operation**, processing over **66 crore transactions daily** and commanding an **84% share** of India’s overall digital retail payments volume.

#### Must Memorize (Statistical Growth & P2M/P2P Split)
* **Transaction Velocity & Volume/Value Matrix:**
  * **Annual Volume Surge:** Expanded from **1.78 crore transactions (FY17)** to **over 24,162 crore transactions (FY26)**  →  Compound Annual Growth Rate (**CAGR**) of **188%** (~13,000-fold surge).
  * **Annual Value Surge:** Increased from **₹0.07 lakh crore (FY17)** to **~₹314 lakh crore (FY26)** (>4,000-fold surge).
  * **Bank Network Adoption:** Grew from **21 live banks at launch** (44 at end-FY17) to **703 live member banks in FY26** (spanning PSBs, private, SFBs, payment, and cooperative banks).
  * **Person-to-Merchant (P2M) Split:** Accounts for **63% of overall volume**, but only **29% of overall value** (routine retail utility).
  * **Micro-Payment Concentration:** Sub-₹500 transactions represent **86% of total P2M volume**.
  * **Person-to-Person (P2P) Split:** Accounts for **37% of volume** and **71% of total transaction value**.
  * **Institutional Leadership:** NPCI MD & CEO — Dilip Asbe | Chairman — Ajay Kumar Choudhary | Headquarters — Mumbai.
  * 🎯 **Recap:** *UPI 10 yrs  •  66 Cr daily txns  •  FY26: 24,162 Cr vol (CAGR 188%) / ₹314 Lakh Cr val  •  703 banks  •  84% digital share.*

#### Know / Understand (Core Mechanism)
* **High-Velocity Micro-Payments vs. High-Value Settlement:**
  * UPI's primary role has evolved into cash replacement for daily micro-commerce ($86\%$ under ₹500), while high-value commercial transfers drive P2P value ($71\%$). This volume asymmetry is why NPCI emphasizes lightweight architectures (UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay) to prevent core banking core system overloads.

ca-rbi-special-usd-inr-forex-swap-facili.title: RBI Special USD-INR Forex Swap Facility: $72.85 Billion Mobilised
ca-rbi-special-usd-inr-forex-swap-facili.atomicRecall: RBI Special USD-INR Forex Swap Facility: $72.85 Billion Mobilised

likelyAsks: Key factual numbers, dates, and institutional ownership

mustMemorizeFacts: **Forex Inflow Mobilisation & Window Timelines:**

The Reserve Bank of India’s dedicated USD-INR Forex Swap Facility, introduced on June 8, 2026, mobilised **$72.85 billion ($72.848B)** in cumulative foreign exchange inflows as of August 21, 2026, propelling India’s headline foreign exchange reserves to **$716.90 billion**.
**Capital Inflow Ladder:**
**FCNR(B) Deposits:** Accounted for the vast majority at **$65.397 billion** (~90% of total inflows).
**Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs):** **$4.860 billion**.
**External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs):** **$2.591 billion**.

**Operational Incentive:** Offered banks a zero-cost principal hedge, regulatory CRR/SLR exemptions, and permitted issuing Standby Letters of Credit (SBLCs) against FCNR(B) deposits (leveraged by Citigroup & Axis Bank partnership).

**Window Adjustments:** Due to rapid target overachievement, the **FCNR(B) deposit window closed on August 31, 2026** (advanced by 1 month), while the ECB/OFCB window remains open until **December 31, 2026**.
**Foreign Exchange Reserves:** Surged by **$9.905 billion** in mid-August to reach **$716.90 billion**.
🎯 **Recap:** *Forex Swap: $72.85B total  •  FCNR(B) $65.4B (~90%)  •  OFCB $4.86B  •  ECB $2.59B  •  FCNR window shut Aug 31  •  Forex reserves $716.9B.*

Implementing nodal ministry or statutory agency

mustMemorizeFacts: **Successor to PLI-LSEM:**

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) notified the 5-year **Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS)** with an outlay of **₹62,500 crore** (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31), succeeding the *PLI for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (PLI-LSEM)* which ended on March 31, 2026.
**Two Target Segments (TS1 & TS2) Ladder:**

**Target Segment 1 (TS1 - Global/EMS Manufacturers):** Open to India-registered firms with minimum FY26 turnover of **₹10,000 crore**. Differentiated incentive of **2.25% to 5.0%** of eligible sales. Existing brands must achieve incremental annual sales $≥ ₹5,000 crore$ above base.

**Target Segment 2 (TS2 - Domestic Indian Brands):** Reserved for Indian brands with minimum FY26 turnover of **₹1,000 crore**. **5% base incentive** + **additional 3% incentive** for domestic design and R&D (up to 1-year gestation).
**Indian Brand Definition:** Trademark & IP held in India, **$>51\%$ Indian citizen control**, domestic design/R&D.
**Component Sourcing Booster:** Up to **1.5% additional incentive** for domestic procurement of camera/display modules, enclosures, batteries, and USB cables.
**Macro Targets:** Projected cumulative production of **~₹39 lakh crore** and **60,000 direct jobs**.
🎯 **Recap:** *MPMS Outlay: ₹62,500 Cr (FY27–31)  •  TS1 (Global): ₹10k Cr turnover, 2.25%-5%  •  TS2 (Indian): ₹1k Cr turnover, 5%+3% R&D  •  ~₹39 Lakh Cr output.*
